pages.title: What it does
text: It is a drop-count multiplier: a stat value of v means m = 1 + v / 100, so v = 100 doubles your drops.
It applies to mob drops and to block drops (drop_rate.apply_to_blocks defaults to true).
Fractional counts use stochastic rounding (drop_rate.rounding = STOCHASTIC): an expected 1.5 items means a 50% chance of 1 and a 50% chance of 2, which is unbiased in expectation.
It multiplies with vanilla Fortune / Looting, whose bonuses are already baked into the drop list before the event fires.

pages.title: Flat (numeric) line
text: The curve is LINEAR: +1.875 percentage points per point.
The old curve, gain = 150 * x / (x + 80), had an initial slope of 150/80 = 1.875, so the early feel is unchanged.

pages.title: Percent line
text: Also LINEAR: 5.0 per point, on the DESIGN_BASELINE basis with reference B_ref = 50 percentage points.
Contribution = 50 * gain / 100, i.e. +2.5 percentage points per point. 20 points -> +50.00; 50 -> +125.00; 100 -> +250.00; 200 -> +500.00.
The two contributions add up to the stat value v, and the final multiplier is m = 1 + v/100.

pages.title: Ceiling & returns
text: Both lines are linear, so the drop multiplier keeps climbing until it meets the attribute's own range (1.0E6, unreachable in practice). There is no designed ceiling and no diminishing returns.

What actually stops you first are two guards: a single event spawns at most 256 items and 64 item entities, and any overflow beyond one stack is split into extra item entities instead of being silently truncated by vanilla.
Randomness is drawn on the server only, so client prediction and the server result stay consistent.

pages.title: Practical advice
text: It feels best on drops that already come in quantity; on a single-item block, +100% is still just one extra item in expectation.
Combine it with experience gain to accelerate resource accumulation noticeably.
Remember it is probabilistic: the same multiplier shows short-term variance, which is expected.
